newsitem.title: UK: Barratt up, Merrill upgrades housebuilders.
newsitem.headline: Barratt up, Merrill upgrades housebuilders.

text.p: Shares in UK housebuilders gained on Tuesday after analysts at Merrill Lynch moved from a neutral to a positive stance on the sector, traders said.

Merrill Lynch analyst Scott Fulton said recommendations on Bryant Group, Barratt Developments, and Westbury had been upgraded to "accumulate" from "neutral", while Wimpey was downgraded to "reduce" from "neutral".
By 1105 GMT, Bryant had gained five pence to 144, Barratt was up 3-1/2p at 255 and Westbury was 5-1/2p firmer at 256-1/2. Wimpey was unchanged at 126-1/2p.
Fulton said expected growth in new house prices was the main reason behind Merrill's more positive stance on the sector.
"We feel new house prices will start to rise alongside the general housing market, which they didn't in 1996," he said.

"If that is the case, housebuilders' gearing to that sort of price increase is enormous. Earnings per share could rise quite significantly and therefore the ratings that these companies trade on are very low under this scenario," he said.
Fulton said house price inflation was also higher than had been anticipated six months ago.
He said all housebuilding shares were expected to perform relatively well but some would underperform the sector, hence the downgraded recommendation on Wimpey.
